messages.subject: Three-way mixed Procrustes ANOVA
parts:
Dear all,

I got stuck in an analysis from a very complicated design. If the team could give me some hints, that will be great. I really appreciate your precious time.

In particular, I am conducting a research which needs a three-way (?) mixed Procrustes ANOVA analysis. After I read the thread “procD.lm and RRPP - how to disable model truncating” (between Mike and Tyler), I followed the suggestions, but I am still not very sure. I am wondering whether the team could help check the code I write below, based on my understanding of the code in that thread, to make sure I am on the right track.

Regarding the analysis, the outcome variable is 2-D coordinates (x, y). The predictors include one between-subjects variable, city (2 cities), and two within-subjects variables, pos (2 positions) and methods (3 different methods). Id would be treated a random effect, that is, those ids were sampled randomly. For one id, theoretically there are 6 sets of coordinates (2 cities by 3 methods), nested with one id. It is of main interest to investigate whether there is any significant difference in those 2-D coordinates between cities after accounting for Age, positions, methods, random effects from ids, and correlation among coordinates.

Here is a toy data set:

   id city Age pos method x_cor y_cor

   1   1   35    L   app1  -0.2  0.1

   1   1   35    L   app2  -0.6 -0.5

   1   1   35    L   app3   0.2  0.9

   1   1   35    R   app1   0.8  0.7

   1   1   35    R   app2   0.4  0.1

   1   1   35    R   app3   0.1  0.7

   2   0   25    L   app1   0.8  0.3

   2   0   25    L   app2  -0.3 -0.5

   2   0   25    L   app3   0.7  0.5

...

"Pos" and "method" are within-subjects factors, and are crossed so I would have 6 sets of (x,y) coordinates nested within each "id". "id" is treated as a random effect.

"City" is a between-subjects factor.

(x,y) coordinates have been processed using Generalized Procrustes Analysis with "gpagen".



My main research question is: is there any significant difference in the (x,y) coordinates between the two cities after accounting for Age, pos, methos, and random effect from id? Random effect from id is of no interest.

Here is the formula I created based on the thread mentioned previously:

 ***

fit1 <- procD.lm(coords ~ (id/(pos:method)) + city*pos*method + Age, RRPP = TRUE, print.progress = FALSE)

Is the formula correct? If not, what formula should I use?

Thanks again for your precious time.

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Three-way mixed Procrustes ANOVA
parts:
Hi Paul, your set up looks to be appropriate to me. Hopefully you have enough observations that you don’t have a degrees of freedom issue to worry about.  You might also be careful about adjusting your anova error terms.  I would also use type III sums of squares instead of type I.  I think you want to make sure that when you’re evaluating your fixed effects, random effects are included in the null model. Therefore, you don’t want term order to have any impact.

Hope that helps!

Mike

Sent from my iPhone
